Enroll in a Portuguese course and give personal details · Enrolling in a course in Brazil means giving personal data: name, nationality, date of birth, address and phone.

Em Brasília: Lendo placas e avisos.

Read common signs and notices · In Brasília you will see many signs: “Pare” (stop), “Atenção” (attention), “Saída” (exit), “Entrada” (entrance), “Proibido fumar” (no smoking), “Empurre” (push), “Puxe” (pull).
Write a short e-mail to a teacher · A short e-mail in Portuguese starts with “Prezado(a)” (formal) or “Olá” (informal) and ends with “Atenciosamente” (formal) or “Abraço” (informal).
Introduce yourself in a longer way · A longer introduction goes: name, origin, age, job, hobbies.
Set a meeting day and time and confirm · In Recife, scheduling meetings requires day, time and place.
Em Porto Alegre: Pedidos e desculpas.
Make polite requests and apologize · Politeness matters.
Em Florianópolis: Minha viagem pelo Brasil.
Tell about a trip using the past tense · Telling about a trip uses the simple past (pretérito perfeito): “Eu visitei”, “Eu comi”, “Eu fui”.
Em Rio de Janeiro: Cem episódios!.
Celebrate 100 episodes and look ahead · You’ve reached 100 episodes of Neighbors Portuguese! You can introduce yourself, order food, ask directions, talk about family, plans and the past.
